extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers and students of literary style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and aesthetic principles for composing literary prose: sentence-level diction, revision practice, moral stance, and the relationship between sensory experience and philosophical expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic temper / reminiscence
rubrics_metrics.description: Though working in prose, retain a 'poetic temper'—a habitual, almost systematic life of reminiscence and reflective apprehension of past impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text describes a writer who lives much in reminiscence and whose imaginative memory presents experiences in delicate perspective; this inward, pensive habit shapes tone and subject-matter and supplies material for expressive prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value the present for its memory-impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape daily experience with an eye to how it will look and be valued in memory ('How will it look to me, at what shall I value it, this day next year?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft scenes and moments so they register as memorable impressions—the main concern in any given day is its impression for the memory; this affects selection and emphasis in narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest and present singular clauses of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to 'arrest, for others also, certain clauses of experience'—to capture and transmit ephemeral sensory moments (e.g., 'imprisoned the very perfume of the flowers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise, evocative detail to fix fleeting impressions for readers; the writer's desire is to prolong a desirable moment a little by exact and literal transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words as objects: transparency of phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 'the word, the phrase' as things whose value is 'in exact proportion to the transparency with which it conveyed to others the apprehension, the emotion, the mood' felt by the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer language that transparently communicates internal states rather than ornate or obscuring diction; clarity of conveyed feeling is the metric of a phrase's worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: True self-understanding as foundation of style
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'true understanding of one's self' is asserted as 'ever the first condition of genuine style.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic style springs from inward knowing; cultivate self-awareness so that diction and tone follow naturally from an honest apprehension of one's impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language delicate and measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer language that is 'delicate and measured' (the 'delicate Attic phrase' is held up as powerful and response‑eliciting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured, refined phrasing can move readers' hearts and even practical responses; avoid clumsy or overwrought language in favor of apt, tasteful expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of grace with intellectual rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a 'rare blending of grace with an intellectual rigour or astringency'—a mixture that yields singular expressiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine aesthetic beauty (grace) with disciplined thought (rigour) in prose so that style is both persuasive and elegant; examples in the text point to valuing both sensibility and analytic clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry, disciplined life, and healthy rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A life of 'industry, of industrious study, only possible through healthy rule' is presented as necessary for the work of the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain bodily and mental discipline—regular study and habits—to preserve clarity of perception and the capacity for sustained literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firmness of outline amid richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the 'logical conscience' produce a certain 'firmness of outline' in literary style—a 'touch of the worker in metal, amid its richness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even rich, ornate prose should rest on a clear, firm structure; sculpt sentences so they have definite form and strength as well as beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and erasure as essential
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'happy phrase or sentence' is 'really modelled upon a cleanly finished structure of scrupulous thought' and the writer 'blamed instinctively alike in his work and in himself, ... all that had not passed a long and liberal process of erasure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorous editing and the willingness to erase are indispensable; excellent phrasing emerges from extensive revision and disciplined pruning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of thought precedes felicitous phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: A felicitous phrase is modelled upon a 'finished structure of scrupulous thought'—thought must be worked into clear form before perfect phrasing follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop ideas thoroughly and clearly before polishing language; precise intellectual structure begets precise language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live in the concrete; record sensory particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate to 'live in the concrete'—to produce 'exact and literal transcript' of what passes around one, trusting concrete sensory detail as material for art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground abstract reflection in specific sensory observation; concrete detail sharpens prose and supplies the images that carry philosophical or emotional weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate sensory data into philosophical scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Let philosophic reflection be 'the reflection of the data of sense'—a reduction to the abstract of the brilliant road one travels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sense-impressions as the source-material for abstract thought; the balance between observation and reflection produces coherent literary philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral responsibility in artistic conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an ethical stance: a determination 'to add nothing, not so much as a transient sigh, to the great total of men's unhappiness' in one's way through the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the ethical effects of writing and public presence; the writer's vocation includes a responsibility not to increase human suffering.
